summary.name: Open Interpreter
summary.one_liner: An open-source terminal coding agent optimized for low-cost and open-weight models, forked from Codex.
keywords: run ai agent on local models
edit code with ai from command line
use_cases: Editing and fixing code in a project from the terminal
Running coding tasks with low-cost or open-weight models
Sandboxed AI-assisted code changes with approval prompts
Using local models through Ollama or LM Studio
summary.what_it_does: The page describes a terminal coding agent that reads files, edits code, runs commands, and asks for approval before going beyond its sandbox. It ships model-specific harnesses for providers such as Kimi, Qwen, and DeepSeek. Built-in providers named include OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock, Ollama, and LM Studio, with hosted providers such as Anthropic and OpenRouter also listed. It inherits AGENTS.md instructions, skills, and MCP server configuration from Codex-style setups. Sessions can be resumed or forked, and a desktop app for documents and browsers is mentioned.
notable: Model-specific harnesses for Kimi, Qwen, DeepSeek and other open models
OS-level sandbox with network and write gating, sandbox mode separate from approval policy
Fork of Codex that supports AGENTS.md, skills and MCP servers
caveats: Hosted models route requests through their servers and are logged for up to 30 days
Desktop app is described as a separate product for non-developers
